reason: Second batch of core timing fixes, recorded while uncommitted: the commit field names the base commit, not a landing commit. What moved: (1) tcenv/bench.py marks every interleaved call with its arm and phase, so the candidate GPU window can be told apart from calibration, warm-up, the candidate_copy_control alias and baseline arms; it also names EXTENDED_ATTEMPTS so the report and its readers share one attempt bound instead of a literal 9. (2) tcenv/backends/metal/v2_runtime.py keeps only candidate-arm readings from repetitions that count, so the Host Program path no longer reports the tail of the last batch and --control no longer shifts the candidate median; a missing timestamp stays missing instead of being written as 0, and the extra quiet attempts are reported as attempts with base_attempts/extended_attempts instead of being clamped to three. (3) tcenv/backends/metal/runtime.py makes per_launch_set_event report the sum of each command buffer's own GPU duration; the end-to-end span is kept separately as gpu_span_s and is not the median input. (4) taic/track_explore.py accepted only attempts <= BENCH_ATTEMPTS for a fresh confirmation report, which after (2) would eliminate a legitimately quiet confirmation as confirmation_batch_mismatch; it now accepts the runtime's real bound and requires any count past the base attempts to carry its own extended_attempts split, while the confirmation retry bound and the single-independent-batch rule are unchanged. The report field can only be written where the report is assembled, tcenv/evaluate.py, which is inside the import closure, so the closure moves from 3971fb38 to e40484f1 with the same 79 files. No prompt bytes, task contract, timing band, warm-up count, attempt schedule, speedup/search-best value or promotion threshold changed; wall-clock ratios, A/A pairing and the 1.10 gate are untouched.
